walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK imports roughly 46% of its food — high food miles raise CO2.

Agribusiness in East Anglia uses big machines, pesticides and irrigation — efficient but environmentally damaging.

Local trends: farmers' markets, allotments, seasonal eating reduce food miles.

Rainfall is uneven: wet NW (Lake District) vs dry SE (London region).

Water transfer: schemes like Kielder Reservoir in Northumberland supply NE England.

Demand is high in the south-east — population dense and gardens water-thirsty. Climate change makes droughts more likely.

The UK has shifted away from coal:

Gas ~40%, renewables (mostly wind) ~40%+, nuclear ~15%, coal ~1%.

Trade-offs: fracking is controversial; wind is variable; nuclear is low-carbon but expensive and produces waste.
